description: Each rating's share is its number of rental transactions as a fraction of all rental transactions.

c.request: Looking at what has actually been rented (each rental traced through its inventory copy to the film, skipping any that don't link up), what share of the rented films does each film `rating` account for, out of the total across all ratings? For the ratings whose share is above the average share across ratings, give one row with: their combined number of rented films, their average share, and how far on average their share sits above that average share. No rounding. Each rating's share is its number of rental transactions as a fraction of all rental transactions.
c.sql: WITH rating_counts AS (SELECT f.rating, COUNT(*) AS rental_count FROM rental AS r JOIN inventory AS i ON i.inventory_id = r.inventory_id JOIN film AS f ON f.film_id = i.film_id GROUP BY f.rating), rating_shares AS (SELECT rating, rental_count, rental_count / SUM(rental_count) OVER () AS share FROM rating_counts), compared AS (SELECT rental_count, share, AVG(share) OVER () AS average_share_across_ratings FROM rating_shares) SELECT SUM(rental_count) AS combined_rented_films, AVG(share) AS average_share, AVG(share - average_share_across_ratings) AS average_amount_above_average_share FROM compared WHERE share > average_share_across_ratings;

b.request: Count rental transactions that join through inventory to a film, calculate each rating’s share of all such transactions, then return one row for ratings whose share exceeds the average rating share: their combined transaction count, average share, and average amount above that average share, without rounding
b.sql: WITH rating_counts AS (SELECT f.rating, COUNT(*) AS transaction_count FROM rental r JOIN inventory i ON i.inventory_id = r.inventory_id JOIN film f ON f.film_id = i.film_id GROUP BY f.rating), rating_shares AS (SELECT rating, transaction_count, transaction_count / SUM(transaction_count) OVER () AS share FROM rating_counts), compared AS (SELECT transaction_count, share, AVG(share) OVER () AS average_rating_share FROM rating_shares) SELECT SUM(transaction_count) AS combined_transaction_count, AVG(share) AS average_share, AVG(share - average_rating_share) AS average_amount_above_average_share FROM compared WHERE share > average_rating_share

a.request: Link each rental to its inventory copy and that copy's film, dropping rentals with no matching copy or film. For each film `rating`, count the rental transactions, so a film rented many times counts each time. Compute each rating's share as its count divided by the total of these counts across all ratings. Keep only the ratings whose share is above the average share across ratings, with each rating weighted equally. Return a single row with: the total count of those ratings, their average share, and the average amount by which their share exceeds that average share. Do not round anything.
a.sql: WITH rating_counts AS (SELECT f.rating, COUNT(*) AS rental_count FROM rental AS r JOIN inventory AS i ON i.inventory_id = r.inventory_id JOIN film AS f ON f.film_id = i.film_id GROUP BY f.rating), rating_shares AS (SELECT rating, rental_count / SUM(rental_count) OVER () AS share FROM rating_counts), average_share AS (SELECT AVG(share) AS share FROM rating_shares) SELECT COUNT(*) AS rating_count, AVG(rs.share) AS average_share, AVG(rs.share - a.share) AS average_excess_share FROM rating_shares AS rs CROSS JOIN average_share AS a WHERE rs.share > a.share

d.request: For rental transactions that link through an inventory copy to a film, calculate each film rating’s share as its transaction count divided by the total transaction count across all ratings. For ratings whose share exceeds the average share across ratings, return one row with their combined transaction count, their average share, and the average amount by which their shares exceed that average. Do not round.
d.sql: WITH rating_counts AS (SELECT f.rating, COUNT(*) AS transaction_count FROM rental AS r JOIN inventory AS i ON i.inventory_id = r.inventory_id JOIN film AS f ON f.film_id = i.film_id GROUP BY f.rating), rating_shares AS (SELECT rating, transaction_count, transaction_count / SUM(transaction_count) OVER () AS share FROM rating_counts), shares_with_average AS (SELECT transaction_count, share, AVG(share) OVER () AS average_share FROM rating_shares) SELECT SUM(transaction_count) AS combined_transaction_count, AVG(share) AS average_share, AVG(share - average_share) AS average_excess_share FROM shares_with_average WHERE share > average_share
